market_context: United States; allergen labeling and dairy products
title: Lactose-Free vs Dairy-Free: Why They Do Not Mean the Same Thing

seo.title: Lactose-Free vs Dairy-Free: Key Difference
seo.meta_description: Lactose-free milk can still contain casein and whey. Dairy-free means no milk-derived ingredients. The distinction matters for lactose intolerance versus milk allergy.
seo.search_intent: Differentiate lactose-free products from products without dairy ingredients.

excerpt: “Lactose-free” can describe a product that is still entirely dairy: the milk sugar lactose has been removed or broken down, while proteins such as casein and whey remain. “Dairy-free” means the product does not use milk-derived ingredients.
content_html:
A carton of lactose-free cow's milk is still milk. That captures the distinction. Lactose is a sugar; dairy describes the ingredient source.

Lactose-free does not remove milk proteins

Lactose-free milk is commonly treated with lactase to split the sugar. Casein, whey proteins, calcium, and the rest of the milk remain. That can solve lactose maldigestion.

Milk allergy is a different problem

Milk allergy targets milk proteins, not lactose. Someone with an allergy should not assume that lactose-free milk, cheese, yogurt, or ice cream is safe.

Read the allergen statement

FDA-regulated packaged foods must identify major allergens such as milk when present. Soy, oat, almond, or coconut beverages are dairy-free by formulation, but their nutrient profiles differ and cross-contact can matter for allergy.

For intolerance, think lactose; for allergy, think milk proteins and formal allergen labeling.

faq.question: Is lactose-free milk dairy-free?
faq.answer: No. It is still cow's milk unless the product is specifically made from a non-dairy source.

faq.question: Can someone with a milk allergy drink lactose-free milk?
faq.answer: No. The milk proteins that trigger allergy remain.

faq.question: Are plant milks always dairy-free?
faq.answer: Their base ingredients are dairy-free, but people with severe allergy should still review labels for ingredients and cross-contact information.
